extracted.intended_audience: applicants, inventors, patent attorneys/agents and other users seeking to file or prosecute patents via ARIPO (Harare Protocol contracting states)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for filing, prosecuting and seeking accelerated examination (PPH) of patent applications through the African Regional Intellectual Property Organization under the Harare Protocol. Covers required documents, filing channels, representation rules, fee provisions, and member-state exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is a set of exclusive rights granted by law to applicants for inventions that are new, non-obvious and industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents are valid for a limited period (generally 20 years). In return, applicants are obliged to disclose their inventions to the public in a manner that enables others, skilled in the art, to replicate the invention. The patent system is designed to encourage innovation by providing time-limited exclusive legal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents required to file an application (ARIPO Form 3 and supporting documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: To file the Applicant has to submit the following: a completed ARIPO Form 3 (Request form), a description of the invention, one or more claims, one or more drawings (if any), an abstract, prescribed application fees or a written undertaking to lodge the fees, designation of at least one state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications may be filed by the applicant (inventor or assignee) or by an authorized representative (attorney, agent, or legal practitioner). Ensure all elements (description, claims, drawings, abstract) comply with ARIPO requirements before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation requirement for non-residents
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation is mandatory for applicants who are not resident or whose principal place of business is not situated in a contracting state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An authorized representative (attorney, agent, or legal practitioner) has the right to represent the applicant before an industrial property office of any of the Harare Protocol contracting states. Ensure proper mandate/power of attorney when filing through a representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing channels and online service features
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be filed directly at ARIPO by: e-filing, email, in person, registered mail, courier. ARIPO Online Service allows online filing, online payment of fees, sending and receiving notifications and general tracking of filed applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-filing carries a 20% reduction of the application fee. Use the ARIPO ONLINE SERVICE for electronic management; follow instructions and supported formats on the portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Contracting States and single-application mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Harare Protocol, an applicant for the grant of a patent can, by filing only one application, designate any one of the Harare Protocol Contracting States in which that applicant wishes the invention to be accorded protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The protocol requires the filing of the application to be made with any one of the Contracting States or directly with the ARIPO Office. There are 21 Contracting States (list provided on the site) — designate at least one state when filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file (directly with ARIPO or through a Contracting State)
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol allows filing with any one of the Contracting States or directly with the ARIPO Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may also file through a contracting state. Choose the filing route that best suits national entry strategy and procedural convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and fee documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A prescribed application fee must accompany the filing or a written undertaking to lodge the fees must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Downloadable fee schedule and ARIPO banking details are available on the site. Note the 20% application fee reduction for e-filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Global PPH is a multi-office initiative that promotes cooperation in patent examination and enables applicants to request accelerated examination across participating offices, building on earlier examination work already carried out elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Global PPH extends existing PPH and PCT-PPH arrangements to any two offices within the Global PPH network, including ARIPO. Refer to 'Guidelines to the Global PPH' for operational details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARIPO/CNIPA PPH filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a PPH request to ARIPO, the applicant must submit the request form 13B and the necessary documents according to the Procedures to File a Request to ARIPO for Participation in the Patent Prosecution Highway Pilot Program between ARIPO and CNIPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachments (English and Chinese versions) specify the precise procedures; likewise, when filing a PPH request to CNIPA applicants must follow the corresponding CNIPA procedures and submit the relevant request form and documents (see Attachments 1–4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Member State exclusions from patent protection (notably pharmaceuticals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ARIPO Member States exclude pharmaceutical products (and in some cases test data or enforcement of rights) from patent protection, with temporal or statutory exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Liberia (pharmaceutical products excluded until Jan 1, 2016 or later extension), Rwanda (Article 23.1(h) excludes pharmaceutical products), Uganda (pharmaceutical products and test data excluded until Jan 1, 2016 or such other period; special enforcement provisions limiting enforceability of pharmaceutical process patents until Jan 1, 2016 under certain conditions). Check the relevant national law provisions before filing or prosecuting pharmaceuticals-related applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARIPO mandate and legal basis (Harare Protocol)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO is mandated to grant patents on behalf of the Harare Protocol Contracting States in accordance with the provisions of the Harare Protocol on Patents and Industrial Designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Harare Protocol was adopted on December 10, 1982 and entered into force in 1984. Consult and download the Harare Protocol text for full legal obligations, formalities, and procedures that govern ARIPO patent grants.
